findings.explanation: The SPL buckets spend per day and feeds the series to `predict`; with a 24-hour window there is at most one or two daily rows, so LLP5 has no baseline and the upper95 band is meaningless. This contradicts the implementation text, which requires a 30-day baseline, and a reader following it would build a non-functional alert.
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages.
findings.suggested_fix: Schedule daily (after the CUR refresh) with a lookback of at least 30 days (e.g. earliest=-30d@d latest=@d), and evaluate only the most recent complete day (e.g. add `| where _time>=relative_time(now(),"-1d@d")` in a reviewed SPL revision) so earlier anomalous days do not re-alert every run.

findings.explanation: `implementation` says the baseline is per account and per service, and `description` says results are grouped by `lineItem_UsageAccountId`, but the SPL runs `addtotals` and `predict Total`, so the anomaly test is on one aggregate series across all accounts; no service field appears anywhere in the SPL. A spike in a small account can be invisible inside the total.
findings.quote: Build 30-day baseline of daily spending per account and service.
findings.suggested_fix: State in `description` and `implementation` that the detection evaluates total daily unblended spend across all accounts against an LLP5 forecast, and that per-account series are only shown for drilldown. If per-account/per-service detection is wanted, describe it as a separate variant requiring a different SPL.

findings.explanation: Billing line items are not produced by health checks or maintenance windows; none of the listed scenarios is a real cause of a CUR spend spike. Real benign causes are missing: upfront RI/Savings Plan purchases and monthly fees (RIFee, SavingsPlanRecurringFee, Fee line items), first-of-month subscription/support charges, credits/refunds, tax, and CUR report re-deliveries that AWS refreshes up to several times a day (duplicate line items if re-indexed).
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `lineItem_UsageAccountId`** — Health checks in `cloud_billing` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with billing-specific false positives: planned RI/SP purchases and upfront fees (filter or annotate `lineItem_LineItemType` Fee/RIFee/SavingsPlanUpfrontFee), month-start recurring charges, AWS Support/Marketplace charges, planned migrations or load tests approved through change management, and duplicate line items from report re-delivery (verify how the Splunk Add-on for AWS CUR input handles updated report versions).

findings.explanation: The second set of Steps 1–5 is a generic template duplicated after the UC-specific Steps 1–4: CUR is delivered to S3 a few times per day, so a 5–15 minute poll is not a meaningful setting, `search` is not an index permission, and the 'vendor admin UI inventory count' and HEC/forwarder troubleshooting do not apply to a CUR S3 input.
findings.quote: Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the duplicated generic block. Describe CUR-specific setup: create the CUR (hourly or daily granularity, CSV, resource IDs optional) in AWS Billing/Data Exports, configure the 'Billing (Cost and Usage Report)' input in the Splunk Add-on for AWS pointing at the report bucket/prefix with sourcetype aws:billing:cur into index cloud_billing, and validate daily totals against Cost Explorer unblended cost.

findings.explanation: The data source never names the actual feed (AWS Cost and Usage Report, sourcetype `aws:billing:cur`) or the fields the SPL relies on (`lineItem_UnblendedCost`, `lineItem_UsageAccountId`), and 'scripted poll' is not how CUR is collected.
findings.quote: Billing data with historical trending Collected via Splunk Add-on for Amazon Web Services (Splunkbase 1876) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: AWS Cost and Usage Report (legacy CUR, CSV in S3) ingested by the Splunk Add-on for AWS 'Billing (Cost and Usage Report)' input as sourcetype `aws:billing:cur` into `index=cloud_billing`; requires fields `lineItem_UnblendedCost` and `lineItem_UsageAccountId` and at least 30 days of history.

findings.explanation: 'cloud billing TAs' is vague and the SPL only reads the AWS CUR sourcetype, so no other TA is needed.
findings.quote: `Splunk Add-on for AWS`, cloud billing TAs — Splunk Add-on for Amazon Web Services (Splunkbase 1876)
findings.suggested_fix: Splunk Add-on for Amazon Web Services (Splunkbase 1876).

findings.explanation: `foreach *` here runs the eval once per column (account series) to replace empty values with 0; it does not iterate over multivalue field values.
findings.suggested_fix: `foreach *` fills empty per-account daily columns with 0 so `addtotals` and `predict` see a continuous series.

findings.explanation: HEC is not used to collect CUR in this UC, while the central `predict` command and the CUR data dictionary are not referenced.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the HEC reference with the Splunk `predict` command reference (https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/Predict) and the AWS CUR line item data dictionary.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `where anomaly="Anomaly"` is applied to every historical row of the search window, so the same past anomalous day re-alerts on every scheduled run; restrict the comparison to the latest complete day. The anomaly test is also on the aggregate `Total` only, not per account.
Cost anomaly on CUR spend is a FinOps/Observability signal; 'Security' only fits the crypto-mining sub-case. Consider Observability.

summary: The core idea (predict LLP5 on daily CUR spend and alert above the upper 95% band) is sound and the TA/sourcetype facts are right, but the prose misdescribes the grain (per account / per service vs. one aggregate Total series), the scheduling guidance (earliest=-24h@h) would starve the 30-day baseline, and the false-positive and implementation text is generic template residue rather than real billing-data causes.
